title: Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party
capsule: The Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party — Syria Region governed Syria from the 1963 coup until the present, but the dataset window of 1967–1973 corresponds to the ascendancy of Hafez al-Assad within the party. Following the disastrous Six-Day War of June 1967, the Jadid faction's grip weakened; Assad, then defense minister, consolidated military-party power and staged an intra-party coup on 16 November 1970 (the 'Corrective Revolution'), jailing Salah Jadid and taking the presidency in March 1971. The 1973 constitution, adopted during and after the October War (Yom Kippur War), formalized Assad's presidential Ba'athist state and marks the dataset's terminal year, when Syria's contemporary governing framework was institutionalized.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Syria's territorial extent in this period is well documented; the dataset represents the governing party's control window rather than any territorial change.
